#### Sweeping the skew bound — stack and heap at every step

**What is being answered.** Where "late" comes from — as one function, `evaluate(lag)`, run at four different skew bounds over the same 9 events.

The line to read twice is in `isLate`: `return c < i`. It compares the **window's closing index** with the **event's arrival index**, and never looks at the event's own skew. That is the mechanical form of "late is a verdict, not a property".

`LAG_MIN` = 141 is derived rather than chosen: the highest event time seen before the straggler (260) minus the window's end (120), plus one. It is far below the straggler's 230s of skew, because the watermark only has to stay under the window boundary.

The animation steps through the code, holding each line long enough to read the STACK (call frames and their locals) and the HEAP (allocated arrays and objects) as they are AT THAT MOMENT. Expand any step to study it on its own.

<details>
<summary><b>Step 1 of 4</b> — the whole heuristic is one subtraction</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch03-skew-memory/frames/step-01.svg" alt="Step 1: the whole heuristic is one subtraction" width="980">

`maxEtThrough(3)` is 130 and `lag` is 0, so the watermark is 130 — already past 120, so W0 fires at index 3. With `lag` = 60 it would be 70 and the window would hold. One subtraction, and it decides when every window in the pipeline speaks.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 2 of 4</b> — "late" is a verdict about the WINDOW, not about the event</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch03-skew-memory/frames/step-02.svg" alt="Step 2: &quot;late&quot; is a verdict about the WINDOW, not about the event" width="980">

`isLate` never looks at `e.pt` or `e.et - e.pt`. It compares the window's CLOSING index (4) with the event's arrival index (7): 4 < 7, so late. Change `lag` and `c` changes, and the same event stops being late. Lateness is produced by the configuration, not carried by the event.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 3 of 4</b> — one second below the threshold is still wrong</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch03-skew-memory/frames/step-03.svg" alt="Step 3: one second below the threshold is still wrong" width="980">

`evaluate(140)` publishes 15, the same as the default. The watermark reaches 120 before the straggler arrives, which is still ≥ 120, so W0 has closed. The threshold is not approximate — it is a single comparison flipping.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 4 of 4</b> — and at the threshold, nothing is late at all</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch03-skew-memory/frames/step-04.svg" alt="Step 4: and at the threshold, nothing is late at all" width="980">

`right` publishes 19 with an empty `lateIds`. Read the three heap rows together: late counts 2, 1, 0 — from identical data. And note 141 is well below id 7's 230s of skew: the watermark only had to stay under 120, never reach back to 50.
